program: Chevrolet Brand Guidelines / AND Chevrolet Campaign Toolkit (Sept 2025, V1.3)

checks.title: Chevrolet Bowtie Logo Usage
checks.description: Primary logo is the three-dimensional gold bowtie, used across the majority of touchpoints. Variations include: Bowtie only, Horizontal Brand Mark (bowtie + CHEVROLET wordmark), Vertical Brand Mark, Horizontal TLD Lock Up (with 'Together let's drive'), and Vertical TLD Lock Up. Always lead with the primary 3D logo.

checks.title: Outlined Logo Restrictions
checks.description: The outlined (2D) bowtie is a secondary mark, only used when production constraints or legibility is an issue. Outlined logo should be used solely over white and black backgrounds, or in rare cases secondary drive colors. Always try to lead with the Primary 3D logo.

checks.title: Logo Modification Prohibited
checks.description: Do not: place the logo over areas where legibility is impacted, create new lock ups, alternate the colors of the bowtie or wordmark, rotate the orientation of the bowtie, outline or add effects to the logo, or alter the typeface or style of the wordmark.

checks.title: Logo Clear Space & Minimum Sizing
checks.description: Clear space around the logo is based on the height of the bowtie wing (unit 'X') on all sides. Minimum sizing: Horizontal brand mark minimum 2 in / 5 cm (150px), Vertical brand mark minimum 1 in / 2.5 cm (78px). Logo must never fall beneath minimum sizing guides.

checks.title: Logo Legibility Over Backgrounds
checks.description: Logo legibility must be prioritized across all placements. When over photos, use darkening/lightening gradients to ensure contrast. When over color backgrounds, ensure full contrast of the brand mark. The bowtie must always be clearly visible.

checks.title: Tagline / Together Let's Drive Lock Up
checks.description: The brand tagline is 'Together let's drive' (TLD) with trademark symbol. Used in Print, Film, OOH, and CRM. Always use English language for 'Together let's drive' in all end tags. Padding between wordmark and TLD tagline should be half the height of the bowtie wing.

checks.title: Co-Branding Lock Up Standards
checks.description: When co-branding with partners or local dealerships, optically balance the Chevrolet brand mark with the partner's. Qualifier taglines should be set in Chevy Sans Narrow Medium. Must follow approved co-branding lockup formats.

checks.title: Chevrolet Approved Font (Chevy Sans)
checks.description: Chevy Sans is the exclusive, custom-built typeface for Chevrolet. Available in three families: Standard (Black through Thin), Condensed (Black through Thin), and Narrow (Black through Thin). Chevy Sans Black is the primary weight for headlines across Brand, Multiline, Truck, and SUV work.

checks.title: Headline Typography Rules
checks.description: Headlines must be set in ALL CAPS using Chevy Sans Black. Large format (OOH/film/print): 95% cap-height leading, -20 tracking. Small format (social/digital/web): 100% cap-height leading, -20 tracking. Subheads: Chevy Sans Medium, ALL CAPS, 90% cap-height leading, -20 tracking.

checks.title: Body Copy and Disclaimer Typography
checks.description: Body copy: Chevy Sans Medium, Sentence case, 125% cap-height leading, 0 tracking. Disclaimers: Chevy Sans Narrow Regular or Condensed Regular, sentence case, 115% cap-height leading, 0 tracking. The primary text color over imagery should be White; Black can be used when legibility cannot be achieved with White.

checks.title: Headline Scaling Hierarchy
checks.description: Headlines follow a scaling hierarchy: Primary (100%) for key messaging or defining feature callouts, Secondary (66%) for 'AND' and secondary messaging in films, Tertiary (33%) for accessory messaging in features. Maintain balance and hierarchy of messaging.

checks.title: Core Color Palette
checks.description: Chevrolet core colors: Modern Gold #F2BC18 (Pantone 7408 C), Black #000000 (Pantone Black C), White #FFFFFF (Pantone White C), Modern Blue #0077D9 (Pantone 2172 C). Modern Gold is at the heart of brand communications. Photography injects vibrancy through environment and vehicles.

checks.title: Modern Gold Highlight Usage
checks.description: Modern Gold (#F2BC18) highlights should be used selectively to add focus and draw attention. Primary use: distinguish and reinforce the AND mnemonic. Secondary/limited use: sparingly reinforce key features within messaging. Do not overuse gold highlights.

checks.title: Chevrolet vs Chevy Naming Rules
checks.description: Use 'Chevrolet' for: formal brand positioning statements, corporate communications, product specifications, legal/regulatory contexts, investor relations. Use 'Chevy' for: consumer-facing marketing and advertising, emotional brand messaging, social media and digital content, brand personality expressions ('Chevy Soul'), casual/approachable communications, connecting with 'Doers' audience.

checks.title: Brand Tone of Voice
checks.description: Chevrolet tone of voice is: Confident (vehicles speak for themselves), Sincere (honest and straightforward, no editorial, no nonsense), Charismatic (real and relatable, serious when it counts but never afraid to make you smile). Tone varies by vertical: Truck = Strong/Undaunted, SUV = Expressive/Energetic, Performance = Powerful/Sharp. EV vehicles adopt tone of their respective category.

checks.title: AND Construct Messaging Framework
checks.description: The 'AND' construct is Chevrolet's storytelling framework connecting product and features to narrative. Use AND to connect: Humanity AND Vehicles, Nameplates AND Features, Problems AND Solutions, Performance AND Purpose. Do NOT: use AND as a crutch, use AND as punctuation replacement, or use AND to create run-on sentences. The AND word in gold is a visual mnemonic for the bowtie.

checks.title: Vehicle Photography Standards
checks.description: Vehicle photos must accurately represent the vehicle. Truck photography: strong and confident, natural lighting, outdoor environments, warm tones. SUV photography: dynamic energy, motion blur, athletic lens, vibrant colors. All photography should feel candid, authentic, and relatable — real human moments with the vehicle.

checks.title: Casting and Lifestyle Photography
checks.description: Photography should feature 'Doers' — real, relatable people who are spontaneous, confident, and active. Lifestyle should feel lived-in and authentic. Avoid overly polished or staged imagery. Vehicle should be shown in context of real life, not isolated.

checks.title: Chevrolet Model Name Accuracy
checks.description: Chevrolet model names must be used correctly. Current nameplates include: Silverado (1500, 2500 HD, 3500 HD, EV), Colorado, Tahoe, Suburban, Traverse, Equinox (including Equinox EV), Trax, Blazer (including Blazer EV), Trailblazer, Corvette, Camaro. Trim levels (LT, RST, Z71, ZR2, Trail Boss, High Country, RS, Premier, Activ) must be accurate.

checks.title: Third-Party Content Separation
checks.description: Non-Chevrolet third-party vendor content, ads, or widgets should be clearly separated from Chevrolet-branded content areas. No competing brand vehicles should appear in Chevrolet sections.

checks.title: Chevrolet Bowtie Required on Pages
checks.description: The Chevrolet bowtie logo should appear on every page of the dealer website's Chevrolet sections. Branding and legibility must be prioritized. The bowtie is the most distinctive brand asset.

checks.title: MSRP Presentation
checks.description: MSRP must be clearly labeled as 'Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price' or 'MSRP'. Cannot present MSRP as dealer's own price. Must include destination charge. Pricing should follow GM legal guidelines.

checks.title: GM Financial Offer Attribution
checks.description: Lease and finance offers through GM Financial must be properly attributed. Terms must match current GM Financial programs. Retail end cards must include: offer descriptors in Chevy Sans Medium (10.5pt, all caps), numerical price points in Chevy Sans Black (60pt, sentence case), offer math in Chevy Sans Regular (14pt, all caps small caps), disclaimer/legal in Chevy Sans Condensed/Narrow Regular (7.2pt).

checks.title: Cash Allowance & APR Offer Formats
checks.description: Cash-only offers: '$X,XXX TOTAL CASH ALLOWANCE' with superscript footnote. Cash + DPA offers: add 'when you finance with GM Financial' with double superscript. Qualifying Cash + DPA: 'For current GM owners' qualifier above. APR offers: 'For qualified buyers / 0% APR FOR XX MONTHS / on most models'. All must include proper disclaimers.

checks.title: Retail Event Logo Usage
checks.description: Chevrolet has specific retail event logos that must be used correctly: Red Tag, Truck Month, Spring Into Adventure, Summer Drive. These branded retail logos drive promotional offerings and must maintain clarity and continuity across retail programs.

checks.title: Chevrolet CPO Program Branding
checks.description: Only vehicles certified through Chevrolet's official CPO program may use Chevrolet Certified Pre-Owned branding. Must follow GM/Chevrolet CPO visual standards.

checks.title: Chevrolet Required Disclaimers
checks.description: All advertising must include required disclaimers per GM legal guidelines. Disclaimer copy should be center aligned to the base of frame. Disclaimers use Chevy Sans Narrow Regular or Condensed Regular, sentence case, same type size leading. Chevrolet is a registered trademark of General Motors.

checks.title: Chevrolet EV Branding
checks.description: Chevrolet EV models (Equinox EV, Blazer EV, Silverado EV) follow the tone of voice of their respective vehicle category (e.g., Equinox EV = SUV tone, Silverado EV = Truck tone). Range and charging claims must include GM-estimated range disclaimers. EV models are part of the full vehicle spectrum, not a separate sub-brand.

checks.title: Chevrolet Prohibited Content
checks.description: Cannot depict unsafe or irresponsible vehicle operation. No competing brand vehicles in Chevrolet-branded sections. No unsubstantiated claims or superlatives. Content must align with brand values: Community, Ambition, Ingenuity, Authenticity. No overly staged or inauthentic imagery.

checks.title: Film Opening and End Card Standards
checks.description: Films must always start with a Chevy bowtie in the first few seconds for brand attribution. Films always end with the full brand mark + 'Together let's drive' tagline. The AND visual mnemonic transitions to the full brand mark animation in end cards. End card VO: 'Chevrolet. Together let's drive.' Always use English for TLD in end tags.

checks.title: Outdated Content Prohibited
checks.description: No expired specials, promotions, or seasonal events (Red Tag, Truck Month, etc.) should remain on the website after they end. All content must be current. No outdated model year references or discontinued nameplates in active promotions.
